summary: This fragment exposes the internal error bus on error_o and instantiates the error-check FSM state register with a hold condition that suppresses state updates when block_swcmd is asserted.
behavior: The combinational output error_o is driven directly from err, so external logic sees the same error indication produced internally without modification (/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_errchk.sv:376-376). The fragment also declares the gated next-state signal st_gated_d and instantiates the sparse-FSM state register macro u_state_regs with reset/default state StIdle, using st_gated_d as the registered next state and st as the current state (/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_errchk.sv:389-391). The next-state input to that register is combinationally selected as the current state st when block_swcmd is asserted, otherwise the normal next-state value st_d is used; this implements a state hold under block_swcmd rather than advancing the FSM (/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_errchk.sv:393-399). Two elaboration-time assertions constrain interface widths: the state and software command widths must match the values assumed by the error reporting logic, and cfg_mode_i/cfg_strength_i widths must remain 2 and 3 bits respectively; comments indicate these widths are tied to error-info field encoding and must be revised together if changed (/home/smy/opentitan/hw/ip/kmac/rtl/kmac_errchk.sv:378-383).

guarantees.property: error_o always equals the internal err signal.
When block_swcmd is asserted, the FSM next-state input is forced to the current state, preventing a state transition through st_d.

security_implications: This fragment participates in control-flow hardening for a sparse-encoded FSM and directly exports error status. Holding the FSM state when block_swcmd is asserted can help prevent software-command-driven state progression under disallowed conditions, and the sparse FSM macro suggests fault-detection intent. The width assertions also protect assumptions used in error encoding; if those assumptions drift, error reporting could become misleading.

assumptions.constraint: The encoded widths must remain consistent with the error-response formatting assumptions: $bits(st) == StateWidth, $bits(sw_cmd_i) == 6, $bits(cfg_mode_i) == 2, and $bits(cfg_strength_i) == 3.
assumptions.bug_relevance: This is a behavior contract: if violated, the comments indicate the associated error info fields would no longer match the implemented signal encodings, causing incorrect or misleading error reporting.

uncertain_points: The exact reset behavior, fault-detection semantics, and any additional guarantees of `PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM` are not visible in this snippet; only its use with state type st_e and reset/default state StIdle is evident.

Comments say block_swcmd would ideally be in an always_ff block as a clock-gating condition, but the implemented RTL uses combinational next-state selection to hold state. Without the macro definition, it is not possible to confirm whether there are any subtle differences from a true clock-enable implementation.
